Priorities & Progress

Eight priorities for District 6, and a progress report on each one every quarter.

During his campaign, T. L. Harris called his early-reading goal “The Third Grade Standard.”

Progress, four times a year

Progress reports are published four times a year, once every quarter, so residents can follow the work on each priority through the year.

  1. Q1First report
  2. Q2Second report
  3. Q3Third report
  4. Q4Fourth report

The eight priorities

  1. Early Literacy and Third-Grade Reading

    Third-grade reading proficiency across Memphis-Shelby County Schools, and what the Board asks about it.

    Early Literacy

  2. Early Literacy Instruction and Structured Literacy

    How reading is taught in the early grades, and which instructional approach the district uses.

    Early Literacy

  3. Early Intervention

    How quickly students who fall behind are identified, and what support follows.

    Student Achievement

  4. School Improvement Goals

    School improvement goals: what they are, who sets them, and how the Board oversees progress against them.

    Student Achievement

  5. Safe and Supportive Learning Environments

    School climate, behavioral standards, and the support available to students and staff.

    Safe & Supportive Schools

  6. Annual Literacy Growth Reports

    Whether literacy growth is reported publicly each year, and in a form residents can find and read.

    Accountability & Stewardship

  7. Quarterly Town Halls

    Regular public meetings in District 6 where residents can raise concerns directly.

    Family & Community Engagement

  8. Public Performance Dashboard

    Whether district performance information is published in one place the public can find and use.

    Accountability & Stewardship

How each report works

Timing
Reports are published every quarter, four times a year.
Sources
A figure appears only when it comes from a published source, and that source is named.
Evidence
Where a document, dataset or official record supports an entry, the entry links to it and shows the date it was last checked.
Control
Each priority separates what a commissioner directly controls from what he can influence and what depends on the district. One commissioner is one vote of nine on a board that acts together.

Sources: MSCS Board of Education; T. L. Harris campaign platform, voteharris901.com (campaign wording only).
